slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The review states that rural primary clinics record on 12 standard paper registers and send monthly summary forms to district HMIS officers, who enter them into the national DHIS2; it attributes this to WHO's assessment and its 2022 field visits, and adds that direct entry by computer or tablet is possible but not what most facilities do.

The review states that no nationwide EMR exists and that digital patient records are isolated pilots: CaafimaadPlus C+ DDS live in 43 south-central facilities since 2024 and RAAD scaling to 40 clinics; the document gives no date for the position, so its publication date is used.
The review describes the digital patient-record pilots as isolated and partner-funded, not scaled as standard across rural clinics; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The review states that national policy, naming an HIS strategy and the EPHS for 2023-26, aims for EMR and a digital HIS, while point-of-service recording in rural clinics stays on paper; the strategy is not cited by title.

systems.tiers: entered by district HMIS officers from facilities' paper monthly summaries

note: An AI-assisted 54-country compilation by Data Landscapers; the file's own header says its country figures are the author's analysis and not sourced fact. The plan:current fact rests on an untitled HIS strategy dated 2023-26. It also reports that 58-70% of districts lack an HMIS officer, which fits no aspect.
